blocks.en: Tacitus reports, that amongst certain barbarian kings their manner was, when they would make a firm obligation, to join their right hands close to one another, and intertwist their thumbs; and when, by force of straining the blood, it appeared in the ends, they lightly pricked them with some sharp instrument, and mutually sucked them.
blocks.zh: 塔西佗记载说，在某些野蛮国王中，当他们做出坚定的义务时，他们的举止是右手并拢，拇指交叉。当用力过滤血液时，血液出现在末端，他们用一些锋利的工具轻轻刺破它们，然后互相吸吮它们。

blocks.en: Physicians say that the thumbs are the master fingers of the hand, and that their Latin etymology is derived from “pollere.” The Greeks called them ‘Avtixeip’, as who should say, another hand. And it seems that the Latins also sometimes take it in this sense for the whole hand:
blocks.zh: 医生们说，拇指是手的主手指，其拉丁语词源源自“pollere”。希腊人称它们为“Avtixeip”，应该说是另一只手。拉丁人有时似乎也把它理解为整手牌：
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: “Sed nec vocibus excitata blandis, Molli pollici nec rogata, surgit.” [“Neither to be excited by soft words or by the thumb.” —Mart., xii. 98, 8.]
blocks.zh: “Sed nec vocibus excitata blandis，Molli pollici nec rogata，surgit。” [“不要因为温柔的话语或拇指而兴奋。” ——马特，十二。 98、8。]
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: It was at Rome a signification of favour to depress and turn in the thumbs:
blocks.zh: 在罗马，按下并转动拇指表示恩惠：
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: “Fautor utroque tuum laudabit pollice ludum:” [“Thy patron will applaud thy sport with both thumbs” —Horace.]
blocks.zh: “Fautor utroque tuum laudabit pollice ludum：”[“你的赞助人会用两个拇指为你的运动鼓掌”——贺拉斯。]
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: and of disfavour to elevate and thrust them outward:
blocks.zh: 以及不喜欢将它们举起并向外推：
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: “Converso pollice vulgi, Quemlibet occidunt populariter.” [“The populace, with inverted thumbs, kill all that come before them.”—Juvenal, iii. 36]
blocks.zh: “Converso pollice vulgi，Quemlibet occidunt popiter。” [“民众，用倒拇指，杀死所有在他们之前的人。”——Juvenal，iii。 36]
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: The Romans exempted from war all such as were maimed in the thumbs, as having no more sufficient strength to hold their weapons. Augustus confiscated the estate of a Roman knight who had maliciously cut off the thumbs of two young children he had, to excuse them from going into the armies; and, before him, the Senate, in the time of the Italic war, had condemned Caius Vatienus to perpetual imprisonment, and confiscated all his goods, for having purposely cut off the thumb of his left hand, to exempt himself from that expedition. Some one, I have forgotten who, having won a naval battle, cut off the thumbs of all his vanquished enemies, to render them incapable of fighting and of handling the oar. The Athenians also caused the thumbs of the AEginatans to be cut off, to deprive them of the superiority in the art of navigation.
blocks.zh: 罗马人免除了所有拇指受伤的人的战争责任，因为他们没有足够的力量来握持武器。奥古斯都没收了一位罗马骑士的财产，这位骑士恶意砍掉了他两个年幼孩子的拇指，以免除他们参军的责任。在他之前，意大利战争期间，元老院曾判处凯厄斯·瓦蒂努斯永久监禁，并没收他的所有财产，因为他故意砍掉了他左手的拇指，以免除自己参加那次远征的责任。我已经忘记，有一个人在赢得一场海战后，砍掉了所有被击败的敌人的拇指，使他们无法战斗和操纵桨。雅典人还砍掉了埃吉纳人的拇指，剥夺了他们在航海技术上的优势。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: In Lacedaemon, pedagogues chastised their scholars by biting their thumbs.
blocks.zh: 在拉栖代梦，教师们通过咬拇指来惩罚他们的学者。
